findings.title: SQL expression feature flag is now a no-op
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` but then returns `false` in both branches, so SQL expressions are rejected even when the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle is enabled. Operators who had enabled the flag to use the SQL expression feature will see all such queries fail with "sqlExpressions is not implemented", while the flag remains present and documented. Either remove/deprecate the flag and its documentation, or make this function honor it; as written the flag is misleading dead configuration and the helper name does not match its behavior.

findings.title: No regression tests for the disabled SQL expression path
findings.body: This PR disables SQL expressions by making `sql.TablesList` always fail through the stubbed `DB.RunCommands`, so `NewSQLCommand` should always return an error. However, no test was added to lock in that behavior for `QueryTypeSQL`/`NewSQLCommand` regardless of the feature flag, and none verifies that the DuckDB-based path cannot be re-enabled accidentally. A regression test would prevent a future change from reintroducing the vulnerable dependency or execution path unnoticed.
